description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent truncation of fenced code blocks (markdown) when resuming a streaming session after a short disconnect. This appears after client-side network bursts from an ephemeral corporate proxy that aggressively buffers and then releases chunks, causing a silent tail followed by a resumed stream that omits closing backticks or duplicates opening fences.
Impact: NoteStream's editor feature shows incomplete codeblocks to end users; impacts formatting and can break downstream syntax highlighting/exec. Occurs for ~0.8% of long-generation sessions for this customer.
Environment: Dedicated tenancy in prod (us-east), serving runtime version 2.8.3, edge-proxy sidecar v1.12.
Observed behavior: When the client (browser behind corp-side ephemeral proxy) experiences a short burst of buffered traffic, the SSE connection is torn (HTTP keepalive closed by proxy) then re-established. On resume, the server sends a resume delta but the client renders a code fence without its terminating backticks or shows consecutive triple-fence markers and a missing closing fence. Websocket path shows similar symptom occasionally but less frequent.
Expected behavior: Stream resume should preserve and re-emit the finalizing tokens so client receives well-formed markdown (closing backticks), or the server should send an explicit end-of-stream/terminal marker that survives proxy buffering.
Steps to reproduce (summary below and also in structured field): see steps_to_reproduce field.
Logs: key excerpts included below.
Notes: This ticket focuses on a client-proxy buffering pattern rather than model text truncation; initial token-level checks show the model produced closing tokens, but they never arrive to the client or arrive duplicated in the resumed delta.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a long streaming completion in NoteStream's editor that includes a fenced code block (~800+ tokens).
Simulate a client-side ephemeral proxy that drops connection briefly and buffers ~16KB before reconnecting (we reproduced with 'mitm-proxy' configured to chunk + delay).
Allow SSE connection to resume using the client's session token and resume offset. Observe client rendering and raw SSE event stream.
Compare server-side trace (request/response tokens) against what client received in the resumed SSE frames.
Repeat with websocket fallback to compare frequency and chunk boundaries.
logs: [2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] api-gateway: resume_attempt session_id=note-999 offset=812 -> routed to node-11
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] serve-rt: resume_delta sent tokens 813-821 but client_ack shows only up to 818
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] client-bff: saw duplicate '```' at 14:02:12 and then no closing fence; rendered as open block
investigation_notes: 03/10: Reproduced locally with mitmproxy pattern: buffer+burst. Server logs indicate model emitted closing backticks consistently; gap occurs between serve-rt flush and client ack after proxy burst.
Hypothesis A: Proxy coalescing + chunk boundary reordering causes SSE event delimiter lines to be merged or dropped (edge-proxy not preserving flush boundaries).
Hypothesis B: Resume protocol's delta window was applied twice on reconnect; client-side patch logic drops the final few bytes when encountering duplicated fence tokens.
Observed that websocket fallback had lower incidence, suggesting HTTP-level buffering (SSE over HTTP/1.1) is a strong factor.
Collected packet captures and compared Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding: chunked boundaries; proxy rewrote some headers in our sim environment.
comments: Ava Patel (2026-03-10): Customer submitted screenshot + session id note-999; they see missing closing fence in editor when reconnect happens.

Miguel Torres (2026-03-11): Confirmed reproduction locally with mitmproxy. Created lightweight test harness to toggle 'flush after event' on edge-proxy; observed that forcing explicit flush removes issue in many cases.
SRE - Priya Sharma (2026-03-12): Checked node-11 metrics — no OOM or worker restarts; small spike in retransmits coincident with proxy events. Suggested instrumenting SSE flush/flush_linger metrics.
Customer (Luis from NoteStream) (2026-03-12): Provided corp proxy config (vendor: FastEdge) — shows aggressive HTTP response coalescing set to 16KB. Requested workaround until fix available.
temporary_mitigation: Advise customer to enable websocket fallback in their NoteStream client (less affected) and to request their network team reduce response coalescing to <4KB. Server-side interim: enable explicit event-level flush on affected nodes (node-11) and add a short keepalive after finalizing fences to increase chance proxy passes final chunk.
resolution_notes: Work in progress: engineering validated that flushing each SSE event reduces incidence. Patch merged to add an optional 'terminal-flush' behavior in serving-runtime (PR linked). Next steps: land patch across dedicated pool, coordinate a controlled rollout with customer, and add automated test that simulates proxy coalescing. Plan to mark as Resolved after 48h of no recurrences in customer's traffic and a config change confirmation from their network team.
